insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (Base Sum Insured + Booster+ Sum Insured + Safeguard/Safeguard+ Sum Insured as per Policy Schedule)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: “We don’t limit your choice. Choose the room you like, but choose judiciously to protect your Sum Insured.”
great.explanation: No daily room rent cap is stated, so you can choose any room category. Higher room costs can still consume your Sum Insured faster, so pick judiciously.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: “Enjoy unlimited Sum Insured. The first paid claim in the life of the policy triggers ReAssure ‘Forever’. Once Triggered it stays for life, provided that the policy is renewed without break.”
great.explanation: After the first paid claim, ReAssure ‘Forever’ gets triggered and then stays for life if you renew without break. This can significantly increase claim-paying capacity beyond the base Sum Insured over time.

great.name: Co-pay
great.quote: “Co-Payment: It is the percentage of admissible claim amount You would have to bear, Rest we will pay.”
great.explanation: Only a glossary-style definition of co-payment is provided, and no applied co-pay percentage/trigger is stated here. That means no co-pay is charged based on this wording, so admissible claims should be paid at 100% (subject to other terms).

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.”
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for the first 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. Claims for PEDs become payable after you complete 36 months without a break.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.”
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months of continuous coverage. After 24 months, these conditions are covered as per policy terms.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident…”
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered in the first 30 days from policy commencement, but accidents are covered immediately. This is the standard initial waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “We will pay expenses incurred on consultations, medicines, physiotherapy, diagnostic tests for 60 days before the date of admission…”
good.explanation: Medical expenses for 60 days before hospitalization are covered if related to the hospitalization. This helps pay for diagnostics and treatment leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “…and 180 days after date of discharge IF these are related to the condition for which hospitalization claim is paid.”
good.explanation: Medical expenses for 180 days after discharge are covered if related to the same condition for which the hospitalization claim is paid. This supports follow-up medicines, tests, and consultations during recovery.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: “Home Care Treatment means treatment availed by the insured person at home which in normal course would require care and treatment at a hospital but is actually taken at home…”
good.explanation: Treatment taken at home that would normally require hospitalization is covered under home care/domiciliary treatment, subject to policy conditions. This can be useful when hospital admission is not possible or not advised.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: “Air Ambulance: Only in case of Emergency. Maximum INR 2,50,000 per hospitalization.”
good.explanation: Air ambulance is covered only in an emergency, up to ₹2,50,000 per hospitalization. Any cost above ₹2.5 lakh will have to be paid by you.

good.name: Modern Treatments
good.quote: “We pay for Modern treatments as specified below:”
good.explanation: Modern treatments are covered only for the treatments listed in the policy. If a newer procedure is not in the specified list, it may not be payable.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Claim Safeguard: We will cover non-payable items mentioned in ‘List I – Expenses not covered’ of Annexure I’.”
bad.explanation: Consumables/non-payable items are covered only under the optional Claim Safeguard benefit. Without opting for it, these items can be deducted from your hospital bill and paid by you.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: “If you opt for a Hospital room which is higher than the eligible room category as specified in your Policy Schedule, then We will pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses…”
bad.explanation: If you take a room higher than your eligible category (as per the Policy Schedule), the insurer will pay only a pro-rated portion of associated medical expenses. This can sharply reduce claim payouts even when the treatment itself is covered.

bad.name: No Claim Bonus
bad.quote: No explicit “No Claim Bonus / Cumulative Bonus increase at renewal” benefit statement found (other than wellness discount and inflation-linked Safeguard/Safeguard+).
bad.reference: Mandatory feature check (NCB/Renewal Bonus) — not explicitly stated
bad.explanation: No No Claim Bonus/Cumulative Bonus increase is stated in the provided extract. That means your Sum Insured may not automatically increase for claim-free years based on this wording.

unclear.name: Restore Benefit
unclear.quote: No restore/reinstatement clause found in the provided policy wording extract. The policy instead describes ReAssure+/ReAssureX and Booster+ mechanisms.
unclear.reference: Mandatory feature check (Restore Benefit) — not explicitly stated
unclear.explanation: No classic restore/reinstatement clause is shown in the extract, while separate benefits like ReAssure+/ReAssureX are referenced. Whether you effectively get restoration (and on what conditions like same illness/unlimited) cannot be confirmed from this quote alone.

unclear.name: Room Type Modification
unclear.quote: “You can as per your lifestyle, choose to change the room category we are offering… You can choose between a Single Private Room and a Sharing Room.”
unclear.explanation: An option is provided to choose between Single Private Room and Sharing Room, but the default eligible room category is not stated here. Your actual eligibility and any impact on claims depends on what is shown in the Policy Schedule.
